purpose: How a gold-plating bench makes color and surface appearance repeatable and honest: mapping karat-color families and the levers that shift hue, agreeing an achievable target against a documented reference and a ride-along witness, judging every batch against a sealed master panel under a defined light with a written tolerance and worst-case-zone discipline, reading hue drift as the earliest bath-health alarm to refer for analysis, and routing appearance verdicts to release, hold or defect referral without ever turning color language into a regulated label claim.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

commercial plating chemistry only, operated per the specific product's technical data sheet; hue-lever directions and operating windows are mechanisms governed by the TDS and the shop's own logged runs, never invented setpoints

color acceptance in a small plating shop is comparative: master panel, ride-along witness and documented customer reference under a defined light; published color-class names (Swiss/NIHS 1N/2N/3N) are shared language, and no universal jewelry delta-E law exists — tolerance is agreed per product

the sibling gates exist and are separate: thickness/adhesion verification proves the deposit and defect diagnosis assigns root cause; this KB refers into both and releases jointly with them, never alone

any tank-side or analysis work this KB refers to is carried out under chemical-safety obligation classes (segregation, storage, labeling, PPE, ventilation, training, emergency readiness) with jurisdiction rules verified; cyanide solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together, never share a drain
exclusions: thickness specification per wear class, XRF and coupon measurement method classes and their limits, adhesion test classes (tape, bend, thermal), batch sampling discipline and measurement record-keeping — the sibling Thickness, Adhesion & Verification KB owns proving the deposit; this KB judges appearance only

defect cause trees for peeling, blistering, pitting, burning, dull or hazy deposits, staining and uneven coverage, evidence-based root-cause assignment, and the strip-and-replate decision with its documented-approval and stripping-safety gates — the sibling Defect Diagnosis & Rework Routing KB; this KB names an appearance mismatch with evidence and refers it, and rework on customer goods proceeds only under that KB's approval gates
performing mechanical finishing or prep chemistry — the surface-prep specialist makes the mirror/satin/matte pre-plate finish; this KB verifies it and sets expectations against it
bath analysis, replenishment, correction and contamination treatment — the bath-chemistry specialist's territory; this KB reads hue drift and refers for analysis, it never doses a tank

approving regulated label terms: 'gold plated', 'vermeil', 'gold filled', 'rolled gold' and karat/fineness statements are compliance classes tied to thickness and fineness thresholds in the selling jurisdiction — verify current rules before any claim; this KB flags claim-shaped language and never approves a label
guaranteed wear-life or durability figures — durability statements to customers are backed by measurement or stated as estimates naming their method, never invented as fact
personalized legal, medical or financial advice — nickel-allergy and chemical-exposure topics route to regulation classes and professional care

competency_questions.question: What does the appearance gate own on this bench, and where exactly does it hand off to thickness verification, defect diagnosis and compliance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COLOR_CONTROL_CHARTER states the owned verdict (hue, gloss, texture, uniformity) and the three referral lines, and APPEARANCE_DISPOSITION shows that release is joint with the measurement gates and that mismatches are referred, never diagnosed here

competency_questions.question: What color families can gold plating produce, and which levers actually shift hue on the bath I run?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KARAT_COLOR_FAMILIES names the NIHS-class tone families and the hardener-class tone tendencies, and HUE_SHIFT_MECHANISMS gives the lever set (hardener concentration, pH, current density, temperature) as TDS-governed mechanisms with directions, not numbers

competency_questions.question: Why does the same gold bath read differently over different underplates or at flash thickness, and what does that bound about what I can promise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STACK_COLOR_CONSTRAINTS explains underplate brightness, substrate tone bleed-through at flash thickness and hiding power of heavier gold, and states achievable color as a property of the whole stack

competency_questions.question: How do I agree a color target with a customer before plating, and what do I do when their reference cannot be matched on the stack they are paying for?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REFERENCE_ACQUISITION requires a documented, condition-noted reference agreed before plating, and ACHIEVABLE_COLOR_ADVISING requires renegotiating an unachievable target honestly instead of accepting it silently

competency_questions.question: How do I make a witness sample that actually represents the job instead of flattering it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WITNESS_SAMPLE_PROTOCOL requires the same stack, same run and same rack-position class, sign-off before production, and a fresh witness after any bath correction

competency_questions.question: What lighting and viewing discipline makes color judgments repeatable, and why can a customer see a different color at home than I saw at the bench?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LIGHTING_STANDARDIZATION defines the fixed light station and names metamerism as the reason judgments and disclosures are tied to a defined light, and VISUAL_COMPARISON_METHOD gives the side-by-side, fresh-eyes, verdict-class procedure

competency_questions.question: When is a spectrophotometer worth using on jewelry, and what are its limits on small curved bright parts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INSTRUMENTED_COLOR_OPTION states delta-E as a method class with an internally agreed tolerance (no universal jewelry delta-E law), its geometry/aperture limits on jewelry, and the eye+panel fallback

competency_questions.question: How is a color tolerance written so acceptance is decided before results exist, and what makes a tolerance realistic?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COLOR_TOLERANCE_AGREEMENT requires anchor, light, zones, verdict method and tolerance written per product before the first batch is judged, bounded by the stack's demonstrated capability

competency_questions.question: How do I judge color uniformity across the recesses, shielded zones and hot edges of one piece?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNIFORMITY_ACROSS_PIECE explains current-density geometry as the mechanism behind paler recesses and hot edges, requires worst-case-zone judgment instead of proud-surface averaging, and separates predictable gradient from defect patterns to refer

competency_questions.question: What is the per-batch color check, and why does it run against the master panel even when every part looks fine?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BATCH_COLOR_CHECK makes the panel comparison a release gate on every batch because color drift precedes thickness and adhesion failures by many batches, and MASTER_PANEL_LIBRARY supplies the sealed, dated anchor that makes the comparison mean something

competency_questions.question: How does hue drift warn me about bath health, and what exactly happens when I see drift on a batch that still passes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HUE_DRIFT_SIGNAL treats visible drift as the earliest bath alarm whose action is a referral to bath analysis before the next batch, and DRIFT_LOG_TRENDING shows how logged verdicts expose slow monotonic drift that single passing batches hide

competency_questions.question: What may I say about color and gloss without making a regulated claim, and which records defend the shop when a color dispute arrives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COLOR_CLAIM_BOUNDARY separates descriptive color-class language from regulated label terms that are verified elsewhere with jurisdiction rules checked, ACHIEVABLE_COLOR_ADVISING keeps promises honest, and COLOR_QC_RECORDKEEPING lists the appearance record that turns a dispute into evidence

competency_questions.question: Why is the gloss and texture the customer sees decided before the tank, and what do I verify pre-plate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRE_PLATE_FINISH_EXPECTATION states that plating reproduces the pre-plate surface rather than healing it, requires a finish-class check before tank entry, and sets the intake expectation accordingly

glossary.definition: Swiss watch-industry gold color class names used across the plating trade as shared, unambiguous language for yellow-gold tone families; a class name describes appearance and is never a fineness statement.

A retained, sealed, dated reference plate or part per product and bath that anchors every comparative color judgment; stored away from sulfur sources so the anchor itself does not tarnish into a moving target.
A coupon or sacrificial piece with the same layer stack, plated in the same run at the same rack-position class as the work; the only sample that represents what the job actually received.
Two surfaces matching under one light source and visibly mismatching under another; the reason every release judgment and every customer disclosure is tied to a defined light.

The instrument-measured color difference between two readings; jewelry has no universal legal delta-E tolerance, so a shop that instruments agrees its own tolerance per product and writes it into the acceptance criteria.

Gradual batch-to-batch movement of deposit color against the master panel; the earliest observable warning that a bath parameter (hardener metal, pH, current density, temperature) is moving, arriving many batches before thickness or adhesion failures.

The published tone tendencies of hardened acid golds as classes: cobalt-hardened deposits lean richer yellow to slightly rose, nickel-hardened deposits lean paler and greener; dedicated alloy baths, not off-window operation, produce true rose or green golds.
A very thin decorative gold layer through which the tone of the underplate or substrate influences perceived color; flash-thickness work can never fully hide the stack beneath it.
The fixed viewing setup — a consistent daylight-class illuminant, neutral surround, set distance and angle — under which every release color judgment is made and recorded.

The lowest current-density area of a piece (recess, inside surface, shielded detail) where color and thickness deviate first; appearance acceptance judges these zones explicitly rather than averaging them away.

nodes.definition: Fix what the appearance gate owns and what it must never absorb: hue, gloss, texture and uniformity acceptance is its own release gate, separate from thickness and adhesion proof (the verification KB) and from cause-hunting when something went wrong (the defect KB). The charter states the deliverable — a comparable, repeatable, documented color verdict per job and per batch, anchored to a physical reference under a defined light — and the three referral lines: an appearance mismatch is named with evidence and referred to defect diagnosis, visible drift is referred to bath analysis, and claim-shaped language is referred to compliance. It also states why the gate exists beyond aesthetics: color is the first thing the customer sees and the earliest thing the bath whispers, so appearance discipline doubles as drift surveillance.

included: owned verdict: hue, gloss, texture, uniformity
referral lines to verification, defect diagnosis, bath analysis and compliance

pros.claim: A chartered appearance gate stops color judgments from being absorbed into thickness checks where they get skipped
pros.example: a batch that measured 2.6 microns everywhere but had drifted visibly rose still gets held at the color gate instead of shipping on its XRF numbers

cons.claim: A separate gate adds a handling step to every batch and tempts consolidation under deadline pressure
cons.example: a rush trade order where the operator wants to call the XRF check sufficient and skip the panel comparison

failure_modes: treating appearance as a subjective nicety instead of a gate, so drift surveillance never happens
letting the appearance gate creep into diagnosing causes or approving labels it has no authority over
acceptance_tests: the charter names the four owned appearance properties, the three referral lines with their receiving roles, and states that release is joint with the measurement gates
revisit_triggers: a sibling KB's scope changes (verification or defect diagnosis absorbs or sheds a check)
the shop adds a service class (e.g. selective plating) whose appearance risks are not covered

base.update_signal: a sibling KB boundary is redrawn or a real dispute reveals a verdict the charter did not own

nodes.definition: Speak color as classes, not vibes: the yellow-to-rose-to-green tone families of gold deposits, named in the trade by the Swiss/NIHS 1N/2N/3N color classes so two people can discuss a target without holding the same part. Hue is an alloying mechanism — cobalt-hardened acid golds lean richer yellow to slightly rose and nickel-hardened golds lean paler and greener, as published characteristics of those hardener classes — while true rose, red or green golds come from dedicated alloy baths, never from pushing a yellow bath off its TDS window. The node carries a hard honesty rule: a color name like '14k yellow' describes appearance only and is never a fineness claim; fineness lives with deposit verification and compliance.

included: NIHS 1N/2N/3N class naming as shared language
dedicated alloy baths for rose/green as classes

pros.claim: Class naming turns 'a bit more gold-y' conversations into orderable, checkable targets
pros.example: a trade jeweler specifying 2N-class yellow for a watch-band refresh instead of mailing adjectives back and forth

cons.claim: Class names compress a continuum, and a customer's mental image of a class can differ from the panel that defines it
cons.example: a customer who calls their target '18k yellow' while pointing at a piece that sits closer to a paler nickel-hardened tone

failure_modes: using a karat-color name in writing where it reads as a fineness claim
promising a rose tone from a yellow bath by planning to run it off its window
acceptance_tests: every bath the shop runs is mapped to its tone family and class language, and all written color names carry the appearance-only qualifier
revisit_triggers: the shop adds or replaces a gold bath system
a supplier TDS revision restates the product's color positioning

base.update_signal: a new bath system, a TDS revision, or a dispute showing the class map misled a customer

nodes.definition: The levers that move hue on any one bath, taught as mechanisms with TDS-governed windows: hardener metal concentration (more co-deposited hardener shifts tone and at excess turns the deposit brownish and brittle), pH, current density and temperature — the published rule for hard golds is hold all four to hold color batch to batch. What matters at the bench is direction and coupling: each lever also moves efficiency, hardness and internal stress, so chasing a color match with one knob can buy the hue at the price of a brittle or stressed deposit. The node teaches what each lever does, how to recognize which lever likely moved from the way the color went, and that setpoints belong to the specific commercial product's TDS refined by the shop's own logged runs — never invented numbers stated as fact.

included: the four hue levers as mechanisms with directions
excluded: numeric setpoints asserted as universal fact

pros.claim: Knowing lever directions lets the bench form a testable suspicion before calling for analysis, sharpening the referral
pros.example: a slow brownish creep on a cobalt-hardened bath raising the specific question 'has hardener metal climbed?' for the bath-chemistry check

cons.claim: Lever knowledge tempts the bench to twiddle parameters to chase color instead of referring for analysis
cons.example: an operator nudging current density up run after run to hold a rich tone while the real cause, pH drift, keeps moving

failure_modes: treating a remembered handbook number as this bath's setpoint instead of reading the product TDS
correcting color with one lever while silently degrading hardness or stress
acceptance_tests: for each shop bath the lever map records direction-of-effect per lever with its TDS window referenced, and contains no bare numeric setpoints asserted as fact
revisit_triggers: the shop's logged runs contradict the mapped direction of a lever
a bath product change or TDS revision alters the stated windows

base.update_signal: shop run logs or a TDS revision contradict a mapped lever direction

nodes.definition: What the layers beneath decide about what the eye sees: a bright, leveled underplate makes thin gold read deep and premium, while a dull or matte underlayer greys the very same gold; at flash thickness the tone of the substrate or underplate bleeds through, so a copper-toned base warms and a white nickel base cools the apparent color of an identical deposit; heavier gold progressively hides the stack but costs metal. Achievable color is therefore a property of the whole stack plus bath, not of the gold bath alone — which is why the same bath produces different-looking jobs and why every honest color promise starts from the stack the customer is actually buying. This node produces the per-stack achievable-color bounds that feed advising, witness planning and tolerance realism.

included: underplate brightness and leveling as appearance mechanisms
substrate tone bleed-through at flash thickness
excluded: thickness class selection per wear class

pros.claim: Per-stack color bounds prevent quoting a match the stack cannot physically deliver
pros.example: declining to promise a deep 3N-class tone on a flash-over-bright-nickel budget job where the white underplate will cool the hue

cons.claim: Stack bounds are qualitative and job-dependent, so they can be argued against by a customer holding one lucky example
cons.example: a customer showing a heavy-build pendant as proof that their flash-refresh bangle can look identical

failure_modes: quoting color from the bath's reputation while ignoring the underplate the job will actually get
blaming the bath for a hue miss that the stack made inevitable
acceptance_tests: each stack the shop offers carries a written achievable-color note naming its underplate effect and its bleed-through behavior at the thickness class sold
revisit_triggers: a new underplate or topcoat enters service
a witness sample contradicts the recorded bound for a stack

base.update_signal: a witness or delivered job contradicts a stack's recorded achievable-color bound

nodes.definition: The gloss and texture the customer will see are made at the polishing bench, not in the tank: plating reproduces the pre-plate surface — mirror stays mirror, satin stays satin, and a scratch plates over as a gold-covered scratch. This node is the check and the expectation-setting, not the polishing itself: before tank entry, verify that the piece's finish class (mirror, satin, matte, brushed) matches what was agreed at intake, and set the customer's expectation that plating will not heal texture, soften scratches or add gloss that the metal underneath does not have. Catching a wrong finish before the tank costs a re-polish; catching it after costs a strip, a re-polish and a replate under the rework approval gates.

included: pre-tank finish-class verification against the agreement
intake expectation that plating reproduces texture
excluded: performing polishing or media finishing (surface-prep specialist)

pros.claim: A thirty-second finish check before the tank prevents the most expensive class of appearance rework
pros.example: spotting an un-buffed firescale shadow on a brass locket at racking and sending it back to the wheel instead of plating over it

cons.claim: The check inserts a stop between prep and tank that pressured runs will want to skip
cons.example: a same-day promise job racked straight from the ultrasonic without anyone looking at the satin panel it was supposed to match

failure_modes: assuming the tank will brighten a dull surface and discovering a grey satin ring where mirror was sold
agreeing a texture verbally at intake with no sample, so the pre-tank check has nothing to check against
acceptance_tests: every job's finish class is written at intake against a named sample or class, and a pre-tank verification of that class is recorded before racking
revisit_triggers: a delivered-texture dispute traces to a missing or vague intake finish agreement
surface-prep changes its finishing repertoire (new media or wheel classes)

base.update_signal: a texture dispute or a change in the shop's pre-plate finishing repertoire

nodes.definition: Pin the target before any gold flows: establish what 'the right color' means for this job as a physical, documented thing — the customer's reference piece photographed and condition-noted with its identity recorded, a retained witness from a previous accepted run, or a named color class tied to the shop's panel — agreed and written before plating begins. The node includes probing what the reference actually is: a solid-karat heirloom reference cannot be assumed matchable by a plated stack under every light, a worn reference has a patina no fresh deposit will show, and a phone photo is not a reference at all. When the target is unachievable on the stack being bought, the answer is renegotiation before plating, never silent acceptance followed by a surprise.

included: reference identity, condition and photo documentation
excluded: intake liability documentation beyond the color target (client-intake territory)

pros.claim: A documented physical target converts the vaguest customer request into something a batch can be judged against
pros.example: photographing a customer's grandmother's bangle next to the shop's 2N panel and writing 'match panel, not bangle patina' into the job

cons.claim: Insisting on documentation before quoting slows the counter conversation and can feel bureaucratic for small refresh jobs
cons.example: a walk-in ring refresh where the customer just wants 'the same gold as before' and no prior witness exists

failure_modes: plating toward a remembered conversation instead of a recorded target
accepting a solid-gold heirloom as the match standard without qualifying light-dependence and patina
acceptance_tests: no job enters the tank without a written color target naming its reference (piece, witness or class), its condition notes and the agreement date
revisit_triggers: a color dispute reveals the reference was ambiguous or undocumented
the customer substitutes or re-describes the reference mid-job

base.update_signal: a dispute traceable to reference ambiguity, or a change in what customers bring as references

nodes.definition: The ride-along witness is the job's truth-teller: a coupon or sacrificial piece carrying the same layer stack, plated in the same run at the same rack-position class as the work, is the only sample that represents what the job actually received — a sample plated separately, at a different current-density position or on a different day, flatters the bath and lies about the job. The protocol: plate the witness with the work, obtain customer or internal sign-off on its color against the agreed reference before committing the production quantity, retain the signed witness with the job record, and plate a fresh witness to re-anchor color after any bath correction or replacement before production resumes.

excluded: witness use for destructive thickness/adhesion tests (verification KB)

pros.claim: A signed witness converts a whole-batch color reject into a one-coupon renegotiation
pros.example: a fifty-piece trade order where the witness came out cooler than the reference and the target was re-agreed before any production part was plated

cons.claim: Witnesses consume gold, tank time and a rack position on every color-critical run
cons.example: a one-off ring refresh where a full witness cycle nearly doubles the job's tank occupancy

failure_modes: plating the witness on a convenient day rather than with the run, so it represents nothing
skipping the fresh witness after a bath correction and discovering the shift on customer goods
acceptance_tests: every color-critical job holds a witness plated in-run at a recorded rack-position class, with a sign-off record dated before production plating began
revisit_triggers: a signed witness and the delivered batch disagree (protocol integrity question)
bath correction, replacement or a stack change since the last witness

base.update_signal: a witness/batch disagreement or any bath event that invalidates the current witness

nodes.definition: The sealed anchor of all comparative judgment: a retained master color panel per product and bath, plus one retained accepted part per batch, each labeled and dated, stored sealed away from sulfur sources (paper, rubber, open air near the polishing bench) so the anchor itself does not tarnish into a moving target. The library is the cheapest, highest-leverage instrument in appearance QC: it is what 'match' means when a batch is judged, what 'drift' means when the log is read, and what the shop shows a disputing customer. Its disciplines are physical: sealed storage, a written index, periodic cross-checks between panel and recent retained parts, and re-qualification of a suspect panel from a fresh signed witness rather than from memory.

excluded: retained parts used for destructive verification tests

pros.claim: A stable physical anchor makes ten different eyes over ten months judge against the same thing
pros.example: a weekend helper matching Friday's batch to the same sealed panel the owner used in March

cons.claim: Panels age even when sealed, and an unnoticed drifted anchor silently re-defines every verdict
cons.example: a panel stored in a paper envelope near the buffing wheel reading warm after a year, making fresh correct batches look cold

failure_modes: anchoring judgments to the memory of last week's batch because the panel is missing or unlabeled
refreshing a panel casually from a random nice part, moving the anchor without anyone agreeing to it
acceptance_tests: every product in service has a sealed, dated, indexed master panel, and each batch adds one labeled retained part to the library
revisit_triggers: a panel-versus-retained-parts cross-check disagrees
a new product, stack or bath enters service needing a new panel qualification

base.update_signal: a panel cross-check disagreement or a new product requiring panel qualification

nodes.definition: Every color judgment happens under the same light or it is not a judgment: a defined-light station — a consistent daylight-class illuminant as an illuminant class, neutral matte surround, fixed viewing distance and angle — because gold hue shifts visibly between warm incandescent shop light, window daylight and cool LED, and because metamerism means a batch and its reference can match under the booth and split in the customer's kitchen. The station is documented (which lamp class, which position), release judgments happen only there, and the light condition is written into every verdict so a later re-judgment can reproduce it. Mixed or drifting light is the fastest way to make honest people disagree about the same part.

included: documentation of the light condition per verdict

pros.claim: One documented light condition makes verdicts repeatable across days, checkers and disputes
pros.example: re-judging a contested bracelet three weeks later under the recorded booth condition and reproducing the original verdict in front of the customer

cons.claim: The station is one more fixed cost and walk-away step, and it cannot reproduce every light a customer lives under
cons.example: a batch passed under the daylight-class booth that the buyer photographs under warm restaurant light and questions

failure_modes: judging at whatever bench light is nearest and getting different verdicts morning versus evening
replacing the booth lamp with a different class and silently shifting every subsequent verdict
acceptance_tests: a documented defined-light station exists and every release verdict records that it was judged there, including the lamp class in service
revisit_triggers: the station lamp is replaced or ages visibly
a metamerism dispute shows the disclosed viewing condition was not communicated

base.update_signal: a lamp change at the station or a dispute rooted in viewing-light difference

nodes.definition: The trained-eye procedure that makes a subjective sense objective enough to gate on: parts clean and fully dry (water films and fingerprints shift apparent tone), compared side by side in near-contact with the master panel or signed witness at the defined light, viewed at the fixed angle, with fresh eyes — color adaptation degrades discrimination within minutes, so long staring sessions are worse than short repeated looks. The verdict comes in classes: match, drift-within-tolerance, or out-of-tolerance; borderline calls get a second checker before any release, and disagreement between checkers is itself a verdict ('hold'). Texture is compared like-for-like: a satin part is never color-judged against a mirror panel.

included: verdict classes and the second-checker rule

pros.claim: A disciplined eye at a defined light resolves differences no casual glance can, at zero instrument cost
pros.example: catching a half-class cool shift on a batch of charms that looked fine in the hand on the way to the packing bench

cons.claim: Even a disciplined eye varies between people and days, and borderline verdicts stay genuinely contestable
cons.example: two experienced checkers splitting on a batch that sits exactly at the tolerance edge after a long inspection session

failure_modes: judging wet or fingerprinted parts and reading a tone that rinses off
one tired pair of eyes releasing a borderline batch that the second-checker rule existed to catch
acceptance_tests: batch verdicts are recorded in the three classes with the checker named, and every borderline verdict shows a second checker or a hold
revisit_triggers: checker disagreement rates rise on a product
a released batch is disputed despite a recorded match verdict

base.update_signal: rising checker disagreement or a dispute against a recorded match verdict

nodes.definition: Instrumented color as a method class, adopted with open eyes: a spectrophotometer turns hue into CIELAB numbers, enabling delta-E trending across months, checker-independent records and dispute-grade evidence — but jewelry has no universal legal delta-E tolerance, so the shop agrees its own tolerance per product and writes it into acceptance, and the instrument's geometry assumptions break on exactly what jewelry is: tiny, curved, high-gloss surfaces smaller than the aperture, where readings scatter run to run. The node teaches when instrumenting pays (repeat trade products, flat-enough zones, drift trending) and when eye-plus-panel under the defined light remains the better method, with the chosen method named in the tolerance agreement so eye and instrument never silently compete.

included: delta-E as an internally agreed tolerance class
instrument limits on small curved gloss parts

pros.claim: Numbers trend where eyes only compare, exposing slow drift and anchoring disputes
pros.example: a monthly delta-E series on a trade product's witness coupons showing a steady warm creep no single batch comparison flagged

cons.claim: On small curved bright parts the instrument produces confident-looking scatter that can overrule a correct eye
cons.example: three readings on a 3 mm domed stud earring spanning more than the product's whole agreed tolerance

failure_modes: buying an instrument and inventing a tolerance after seeing which numbers the process produces
measuring a curved zone the aperture cannot average and archiving noise as evidence
acceptance_tests: if an instrument is in use, each instrumented product names its agreed delta-E tolerance, its measurement zone, and the fallback method for parts the geometry defeats
revisit_triggers: instrument readings and defined-light eye verdicts diverge repeatedly on a product
a product's geometry or gloss class changes

base.update_signal: repeated eye/instrument divergence or a geometry change in an instrumented product

nodes.definition: Write what 'accepted' means before the first result exists, because criteria invented after seeing results always pass: a per-product written color tolerance naming its anchor (which panel or witness), its light (the defined station), its zones (including the worst-case zones by name), its verdict method (eye classes or an agreed delta-E) and its width — a width negotiated against the stack's demonstrated capability, not against hope. A tolerance tighter than the process can repeat converts normal batch variation into permanent conflict; a tolerance looser than the customer's eye converts releases into returns. The agreement is signed into the job or product file and is the sole standard the batch check and the disposition are allowed to use.

included: anchor, light, zones, method and width written per product

pros.claim: A frozen written tolerance makes every later verdict fast, defensible and identical across checkers
pros.example: a repeat trade order released in minutes because the tolerance row already says which panel, which light, which zones and how far is far

cons.claim: Freezing a tolerance before production risks freezing a wrong one that must then be formally renegotiated
cons.example: a first-run product whose agreed width proves tighter than the stack repeats, throwing honest batches into hold until re-agreement

failure_modes: widening the tolerance verbally at the bench to pass a batch that misses it
writing a tolerance with no zone map so recesses get judged by proud-surface standards or not at all
acceptance_tests: every color-critical product or job holds a written tolerance naming anchor, light, zones, method and width, dated before its first batch verdict
revisit_triggers: the drift log shows a product repeatedly borderline against its width
the customer, stack or verdict method changes

base.update_signal: repeated borderline verdicts against a width, or a change of customer, stack or method

nodes.definition: One piece, one color — against the physics that wants otherwise: current-density geometry makes recesses, inside surfaces and shielded details plate leaner and read paler, while edges, tips and points run hot and can darken first; the same mechanism that makes low-current-density zones the thin spots for the measurement KB makes them the pale spots here. Appearance acceptance therefore judges the worst-case zones by name rather than averaging the proud surfaces, and distinguishes the predictable geometry gradient (bounded by the per-zone tolerance) from a defect pattern — blotches, banding, cloud lines — which is not a uniformity question at all but an appearance mismatch to name and refer. Piece-to-piece agreement inside one run and rack position is judged the same way.

included: geometry gradient versus defect pattern distinction
excluded: fixturing, shielding and auxiliary-anode countermeasures (process execution)

pros.claim: Worst-zone judgment catches what the customer's finger and eye will find at home
pros.example: the inside curve of a signet ring reading a class paler than the face — visible the first time the owner takes it off

cons.claim: Some recess zones physically cannot match the proud surface on a given stack, and judging them invites unwinnable perfectionism
cons.example: the deep undercut of a filigree pendant that no rack orientation on the offered stack will bring inside a face-tight tolerance

failure_modes: averaging the piece by its best surfaces and shipping pale recesses
treating a banding defect as 'just geometry' and releasing what diagnosis should have seen
acceptance_tests: each product's tolerance names its worst-case zones and each batch verdict shows those zones were judged, with gradient-versus-pattern noted
revisit_triggers: a customer return traces to a zone the map did not name
process execution changes fixturing or shielding for a product

base.update_signal: a return on an unmapped zone or a fixturing change that moves the current-density map

nodes.definition: The every-batch gate that no good-looking batch skips: first article and batch sample compared against the master panel at the defined light, against the written tolerance, worst-case zones included, before any part moves to stock or shipping — run even when every part 'looks fine' in the hand, because color drift against the panel is the earliest drift alarm the shop owns and precedes thickness and adhesion failures by many batches. The verdict (match / drift-within-tolerance / out) is logged with checker and light condition as one batch-record row; a drift-within-tolerance verdict releases the batch but arms the drift signal; skipping the check converts a future customer complaint into an unsolvable mystery.

included: first-article and batch comparison vs panel
excluded: the bath analysis the drift may trigger

pros.claim: A minutes-long panel check per batch buys the shop its earliest possible warning of bath movement
pros.example: a faint warm shift on an otherwise perfect batch of chains flagging hardener drift weeks before any part would have failed a measurement

cons.claim: It is the check most skipped under deadline pressure precisely because the parts in hand look fine
cons.example: a Friday-evening trade pickup where the panel walk feels like ceremony and the drift goes unlogged

failure_modes: releasing on hand-look without the panel and losing the drift baseline
logging 'pass' without the zone checks so the row certifies less than it claims
acceptance_tests: every batch shows a color-verdict row (verdict class, checker, light, zones judged) dated before the batch moved to stock
revisit_triggers: any missed-batch gap discovered in the color log
a drift or dispute arises on a batch whose row is incomplete

base.update_signal: a gap in the batch color log or a dispute on an incompletely logged batch

nodes.definition: Read the bath through its color: hue drift against the master panel is the earliest bath-health signal a small shop owns — it moves before thickness, adhesion or brightness fail, because the deposit's tone responds to hardener metal, pH, current density and temperature excursions ahead of its mechanical properties. The drift direction, read against the lever map, sharpens a suspicion (a brownish creep on a cobalt-hardened bath asks the hardener-concentration question; a paling drift asks about current density or temperature), but the action is always a referral, never a correction: visible drift means bath analysis by the bath-chemistry role before the next batch, carried out under the product TDS and the chemical-safety obligation classes. This KB never doses a tank, and a drift on a passing batch is still a fired alarm.

excluded: performing analysis, dosing or carbon treatment (bath chemistry)

pros.claim: Acting on drift while parts still pass converts a future whole-batch failure into one bath check
pros.example: a hardener top-up prompted by two batches of faint rose creep, instead of a week of brittle brownish rejects later

cons.claim: Drift calls on passing batches cost analyses that sometimes find nothing actionable
cons.example: a perceived cool shift that the titration and Hull-cell check trace to a new booth lamp, not the bath

failure_modes: ignoring drift because every individual batch still passes tolerance
twiddling bath parameters at the bench instead of referring for analysis
acceptance_tests: every drift verdict in the log shows a referral record (what was suspected, who analyzes) dated before the next batch of that bath ran
revisit_triggers: analysis results contradict the direction-suspicion the lever map produced
drift recurs immediately after a completed correction

base.update_signal: an analysis result that confirms or contradicts a drift-direction suspicion

nodes.definition: Make slow drift visible: one color-verdict row per batch — verdict class, direction if any, bath identity and age, job reference — kept as a running log, because a monotonic creep of small shifts that each pass tolerance is invisible batch by batch and obvious across ten rows. The log ties every appearance verdict to the bath state that produced it, turning 'the gold has looked warmer lately' from a feeling into a dated series; it is also the shop's evidence when a customer dispute asks what the color was in March and what bath it came from. Trend triggers are written down (for example, same-direction drift on consecutive batches fires the analysis referral even though every batch passed) so the log acts, rather than merely remembers.

included: per-batch verdict rows tied to bath identity and age
written trend triggers that fire referrals

pros.claim: A dated series catches the drift pattern that no single honest verdict can see
pros.example: five consecutive 'pass, slightly warm' rows on one bath firing the trend trigger while every individual batch was releasable

cons.claim: A log only works if filled at judgment time, and back-filled rows quietly poison the series
cons.example: three batches logged from memory on Monday, flattening the very drift the log existed to show

failure_modes: keeping verdicts in heads and finding no series when the dispute or the drift question arrives
logging verdicts without bath identity so trends cannot be tied to a tank
acceptance_tests: the log holds one row per batch with verdict, direction, bath identity and date, and a written trend trigger exists per bath
revisit_triggers: a trend trigger fires
a dispute requires reconstructing a past batch's color context

base.update_signal: a fired trend trigger or a dispute that tests the log's completeness

nodes.definition: Honest talk about color, before money changes hands: tell the customer what this stack and bath can and cannot deliver — that a plated deposit may not match a solid-karat heirloom under every light (metamerism disclosed in plain words), that a flash coat will show the stack's tone through it, that gloss follows the pre-plate finish, and that plated color lives in a thin layer whose appearance changes with wear over time, stated as an expectation class with any durability statement either backed by measurement or named as an estimate with its method — never an invented wear-life figure. Plated goods are never represented as solid gold. When the desired color is outside the stack's bounds, the honest moves are: propose a stack that can (at its price), propose the nearest achievable class with a witness to approve, or decline — never accept and hope.

included: achievability advice bounded by the stack
metamerism and wear-appearance disclosure as expectation classes
excluded: regulated label wording (claim boundary and compliance)

pros.claim: Honest bounds before plating convert impossible jobs into either better-specified jobs or clean declines
pros.example: upgrading a flash refresh to a heavier build with the customer's eyes open, after showing why the flash cannot hide the nickel-white cool cast

cons.claim: Honesty about limits loses some jobs to shops willing to promise anything
cons.example: a customer taking their heirloom-match request to a competitor who says yes and delivers a mismatch six weeks later

failure_modes: promising an exact match to a solid-gold reference to close the sale
quoting a wear-life figure invented on the spot instead of a method-named estimate
acceptance_tests: every color-critical quote records the achievability advice given (achievable class, disclosed limits, chosen option), and no written promise exceeds the stack's recorded bounds
revisit_triggers: a delivered job disappoints despite following the advice (bounds need re-deriving)
a new stack changes what can honestly be offered

base.update_signal: a disappointment following per-advice work, or a stack change moving the honest offer

nodes.definition: The hard boundary where color talk stops and regulated claims begin: 'gold plated', 'vermeil', 'gold filled', 'rolled gold' and any karat or fineness statement are compliance classes tied to thickness and fineness thresholds that vary by selling jurisdiction and must be verified as current rules before any label or ad copy uses them — and satisfying them is proven by the measurement KB's verified thickness and fineness, never by how the piece looks. This node's discipline is recognition and routing: appearance language (tone family, NIHS class, gloss class) is free to use; claim-shaped language in quotes, invoices, listings or customer chat is flagged and routed to verification and compliance; and this specialist flags claims — it never approves them. The asymmetry is deliberate: a wrong color adjective costs an apology, a wrong regulated term costs a legal problem.

included: routing claims to verification and compliance with jurisdiction-check flag
excluded: the thickness/fineness verification that substantiates a claim

pros.claim: A recognition-and-routing rule lets the bench talk color richly without ever wandering into label law
pros.example: an online listing draft saying '2N-class yellow tone' passing, while 'vermeil' on the same draft gets flagged for the compliance check because the base metal and thickness were never verified for it

cons.claim: Routing every claim-shaped phrase adds friction to marketing and quoting language
cons.example: a trade customer's own ad copy waiting on a compliance check the shop cannot skip just to be agreeable

failure_modes: letting 'vermeil' or a karat claim ride into an invoice because the color looked right
treating a threshold remembered from one market as valid in another jurisdiction
acceptance_tests: all outgoing written material with regulated terms shows a verification-and-compliance routing record, and no approval of such a term originates from this role
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction rule change or a new selling market
a flagged claim turns out to have shipped unrouted

base.update_signal: a rule change in a selling jurisdiction or a claim that escaped routing

nodes.definition: Route the verdict, do not stretch it: a match verdict releases only jointly with the measurement gates — a beautiful color never releases a batch that has not passed its thickness and adhesion checks; a borderline verdict holds for the second checker or the agreed instrument; an out-of-tolerance verdict is named with its evidence — which zone, which rack position, which batch in the sequence, against which anchor, under which light — and referred to defect diagnosis and rework routing, because cause trees, strip-and-replate decisions and their documented-approval and stripping-safety gates live there, not here. The evidence packet matters: 'it looks wrong' is not referrable, 'recesses two classes pale on all pieces from the lower rack, batch three of the bath week' is. And the default posture is codified: the diagnosis will be assigned by evidence in prep, chemistry or process — never by blaming the customer's piece by default.

excluded: strip-and-replate decision and its approval/safety gates

pros.claim: A located, evidenced referral lets diagnosis start from where and when instead of from scratch
pros.example: noting that only the lower-rack pieces of the day's third batch went pale, pointing diagnosis straight at a current-distribution question

cons.claim: Strict routing means the appearance bench sometimes holds work it feels sure it could fix itself
cons.example: an operator confident the haze would buff out, waiting on the diagnosis path the charter requires

failure_modes: releasing on color while a measurement gate is still open
referring 'looks wrong' with no location, timing or anchor evidence
acceptance_tests: every disposition shows one of release-joint/hold/refer, and every referral carries zone, position, batch-sequence, anchor and light evidence
revisit_triggers: a referral bounces back for missing evidence
a released batch is disputed on a property the disposition did not check

base.update_signal: a bounced referral or a dispute on an unchecked property

nodes.definition: The appearance record that turns a dispute from memory-versus-memory into evidence: per job and batch — the documented reference identity and its condition photos, the signed witness and its sign-off date, the written tolerance in force, the light condition and lamp class at judgment, the verdict with checker and zones judged, defect-referral packets if any, photos of anything contested, and the pointer to the batch's retained part in the library. Kept at judgment time, not reconstructed later; retained through the product's dispute horizon; and deliberately scoped to appearance — thickness, adhesion and sampling records belong to the verification KB, and the two records cross-reference by job number rather than duplicating each other.

included: reference, witness, tolerance, light, verdict, photos, retained-part pointer
cross-reference to measurement records by job

pros.claim: A complete appearance record ends most disputes at the folder, before they reach an argument
pros.example: answering 'it was never this pink' by producing the signed witness, the booth photo and the customer's own sign-off date

cons.claim: Record discipline is unpaid minutes on every batch, and the value shows only on the rare bad day
cons.example: a year of diligent rows never opened until the one trade claim that they settle in five minutes

failure_modes: reconstructing records after a dispute starts, which convinces nobody
duplicating measurement data into the appearance record until neither record is authoritative
acceptance_tests: a spot-checked job can produce reference, witness sign-off, tolerance, verdict row, light condition and retained-part pointer from its record alone
revisit_triggers: a spot-check finds a gap
a dispute exercises the record and reveals a missing element

base.update_signal: a record spot-check gap or a dispute that finds the record wanting

edges.why_related: the shared color language is built to serve the verdict the charter defines
the charter's comparable-verdict promise is physically kept by the sealed anchor library
the charter's repeatable-verdict promise requires one defined light for all judgments
lever directions are stated relative to the tone families the class map names
stack bounds are expressed in the class language the family map establishes
a named color class is one of the three legitimate reference forms
the witness is signed off against the documented reference, so the reference must exist first
a representative witness must carry the job's actual stack, which the bounds identify as color-decisive
the side-by-side procedure is only valid at the defined light station
the comparison needs the sealed panel as its anchor object
the instrument is adopted as an extension of, and fallback to, the working eye procedure
the tolerance names its anchor, which the documented reference supplies
which zones deviate and how far is set by the stack and geometry mechanisms the bounds describe
the batch gate judges only against the frozen written tolerance
drift is read from the batch-by-batch panel comparisons the gate produces
the log's rows are the batch gate's recorded verdicts
honest advice is bounded by the per-stack achievable-color notes
gloss and texture promises rest on what the pre-plate finish will actually be
disposition routes the verdict the batch gate produced
the record captures the disposition and its evidence packet as part of the job file
the finish class is verified before the witness plates, or the witness shows a texture the job will not have
the signed witness demonstrates capability, and the tolerance width is frozen only after that demonstration
worst-case zones are judged before the disposition, or the release certifies surfaces nobody looked at
advising language must stay descriptive; claim-shaped wording is flagged and routed, never spoken as approval
no batch verdict counts unless judged at the defined light station
disposition may only apply the pre-agreed tolerance, never a widened bench version of it
records describe appearance in class language and must not certify regulated terms the role cannot approve
parameter movement causes visible hue movement first, which is exactly why drift reads bath health early
surface texture changes perceived hue and gloss, forcing the like-for-like texture rule in comparison
geometry-driven zone variation limits the uniformity that can honestly be promised on complex pieces
after a drift-triggered bath correction, a fresh witness re-anchors color before production resumes
logged trend evidence is what justifies renegotiating a tolerance that proves unrealistic or slack
each released batch deposits its retained part, keeping the anchor library current
instrument delta-E and the trained eye can disagree, especially on small curved gloss parts where readings scatter
edges.resolution_rule: the method named in the product's written tolerance agreement decides; on genuine unresolved disagreement the batch holds for a second defined-light check, and geometry the aperture cannot average defaults to eye-plus-panel

edges.why_related: a batch can pass its tolerance while showing drift, pitting release throughput against the alarm's demand to pause
edges.resolution_rule: release what passes the written tolerance, but the drift referral fires anyway: bath analysis before the next batch of that bath, and the alarm is never suppressed because parts still pass

edges.why_related: the customer's documented reference can demand a color the stack cannot deliver, opposing the wish to accept the job as specified
edges.resolution_rule: achievability wins before plating: renegotiate to a stack that can, to the nearest achievable class approved on a witness, or decline — an unachievable target is never accepted silently

edges.why_related: a width tight enough for proud surfaces can be physically unreachable in recesses on the offered stack
edges.resolution_rule: the tolerance is written per zone with worst-case zones named; if a named zone cannot meet its width on the stack, the width or the stack changes before production, never the judging standard at the bench

edges.why_related: both are physical comparison anchors: the panel anchors a product's ongoing color, the witness anchors one job's agreed color

conflict_axes.name: throughput_vs_drift_alarm
conflict_axes.description: Passing batches want to ship on schedule while a visible drift on those same batches demands a bath-analysis pause before the next run.
poles: release passing work and keep the line moving
pause the bath on the earliest drift signal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: release what passes the written tolerance, but fire the analysis referral before the next batch of that bath — the alarm is never traded for schedule

conflict_axes.name: customer_reference_vs_stack_reality
conflict_axes.description: The reference the customer loves may be outside what their chosen stack can deliver, and saying so risks the sale.
poles: accept the job as the customer specified it
advise only what the stack can honestly achieve
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: renegotiate before plating: a capable stack at its price, the nearest achievable class approved on a witness, or a clean decline

conflict_axes.name: trained_eye_vs_instrument_number
conflict_axes.description: The eye reads whole-piece appearance the aperture cannot, while the instrument trends and testifies in ways the eye cannot.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the method written into the product's tolerance agreement decides, with eye-plus-panel as the default for geometry that defeats the aperture

conflict_axes.name: tight_tolerance_vs_process_capability
conflict_axes.description: Sales wants to promise an exact match; the stack and bath have a natural batch-to-batch spread that a too-tight width turns into permanent conflict.
poles: write a width the process can repeat
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: freeze a capability-bounded width demonstrated by the witness, and renegotiate formally when the drift log shows the width is wrong

conflict_axes.name: judgment_speed_vs_lighting_discipline
conflict_axes.description: The nearest bench light gives an instant answer; the defined-light station gives a repeatable one a walk away.
poles: judge only at the defined light
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hand-look freely for gross problems, but no release verdict exists until the panel comparison happens at the station

conflict_axes.name: descriptive_color_talk_vs_regulated_claims
conflict_axes.description: Rich color language sells, and one step further it becomes a regulated label term the role has no authority to grant.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tone-family and class language flows freely; anything claim-shaped is flagged and routed to verification and compliance with jurisdiction rules checked

conflict_axes.name: panel_stability_vs_panel_refresh
conflict_axes.description: An old sealed panel is a stable anchor that slowly ages; refreshing it re-defines 'match' for every later verdict.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cross-check panel against recent retained parts on a cadence; re-qualify from a fresh signed witness as a recorded event, never casually

conflict_axes.name: uniformity_ideal_vs_geometry_physics
conflict_axes.description: The customer expects one color everywhere; current-density geometry pales recesses and heats edges on every complex piece.
poles: hold every zone to the face standard
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: name the worst-case zones and give them their own agreed width; refer true out-of-band zones, and disclose the gradient honestly on complex geometry

conflict_axes.name: record_burden_vs_dispute_defense
conflict_axes.description: Appearance records cost minutes on every batch and prove their worth only on the rare day a dispute or drift question arrives.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the short mandatory row (verdict, checker, light, anchor, retained part) always, and the fuller packet for color-critical and customer-goods jobs

edge_cases.description: The customer's reference is a solid 18k heirloom whose hue no plated stack will match under every light
edge_cases.trigger: a solid-karat reference piece is presented as the match standard
edge_cases.mitigation: disclose metamerism and patina limits in plain words, agree the match on a witness under the defined light, and record that the agreement is to the witness, not the heirloom

edge_cases.description: A batch matched the panel at the booth but the customer sees a different color under warm home lighting
edge_cases.mitigation: re-judge with the customer under the recorded booth condition, show the disclosed light-dependence note from the job record, and treat it as a disclosure lesson if none exists

edge_cases.description: The master panel itself has tarnished in storage, so fresh correct batches read warm against a drifted anchor
edge_cases.trigger: panel aging from sulfur exposure or unsealed storage
edge_cases.mitigation: cross-check the panel against recent retained parts; if the panel moved, re-qualify it from a fresh signed witness as a recorded event before judging further batches

edge_cases.description: The recesses of a filigree piece read two classes paler than its proud surfaces
edge_cases.trigger: low current-density zones on complex geometry
edge_cases.mitigation: judge against the named worst-case-zone width; inside it, disclose the gradient; outside it, refer with zone evidence rather than shipping on the face color

edge_cases.description: A brownish cast appears at edges and tips on an otherwise passing batch
edge_cases.trigger: edge darkening that could be hardener drift or a burning-class process problem
edge_cases.mitigation: log the drift observation with its location evidence, refer to bath analysis and to defect diagnosis in parallel, and do not release until the pattern is classified

edge_cases.description: Two experienced checkers split on a borderline batch at the end of a long inspection day
edge_cases.trigger: checker disagreement on a tolerance-edge verdict
edge_cases.mitigation: disagreement is a hold verdict: fresh eyes next session, the agreed instrument if the product names one, and no release on a tie

edge_cases.description: A customer asks 'so is this 18k gold?' at handover of a plated piece
edge_cases.trigger: a color-class name being heard as a fineness claim
edge_cases.mitigation: answer in appearance language ('18k-style yellow tone, gold plating over the base metal'), never affirm fineness, and route any written karat wording to verification and compliance

edge_cases.description: A satin bangle and a mirror ring from the same run look like different golds to the customer
edge_cases.trigger: texture-driven perceived color difference within one bath run
edge_cases.mitigation: compare like texture to like texture only, and set the intake expectation that finish class changes apparent tone even from an identical deposit

edge_cases.description: The witness was plated a day earlier at a different rack position and disagrees with the delivered batch
edge_cases.trigger: a non-representative witness discovered after a color complaint
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the witness as void, re-anchor with a true ride-along on the remake, and tighten the protocol record to require run and rack-position entries

edge_cases.description: The batch color check is skipped on a rush order because every part looks fine in the hand
edge_cases.trigger: deadline pressure against the panel-comparison gate
edge_cases.mitigation: the check is a release gate, not a courtesy: minutes at the station beat an unlogged drift discovered three batches later as a reject pile

edge_cases.description: Five consecutive batches each pass tolerance while the log shows a monotonic warm creep on one bath
edge_cases.trigger: a written trend trigger firing on passing batches
edge_cases.mitigation: the trend fires the analysis referral exactly as a single visible drift would; passing batches ship, the bath gets checked before the next run

edge_cases.description: The spectrophotometer returns scattered readings on a tiny domed stud earring
edge_cases.trigger: part geometry smaller and rounder than the instrument aperture assumes
edge_cases.mitigation: fall back to eye-plus-panel at the defined light per the tolerance agreement, and record the method used so the file shows why no number exists

workflow.description: State the owned verdict (hue, gloss, texture, uniformity), the joint-release rule and the three referral lines
workflow.gate: verdict scope, joint release and referral lines to verification, defect diagnosis, bath analysis and compliance are written

workflow.action: Map the shop's color families and hue levers
workflow.description: Tie every bath in service to its tone family, class language and TDS-referenced lever directions
workflow.artifact: per-bath color family and lever map
workflow.gate: each bath shows family, class names and lever directions with no bare setpoints asserted as fact

workflow.action: Bound achievable color per offered stack
workflow.description: Write what each stack's underplate and thickness class do to perceived color
workflow.gate: every offered stack carries its written color bound including flash bleed-through behavior

workflow.description: Fix illuminant class, surround, distance and angle, and document them
workflow.gate: the station and its lamp class are documented and all release judgments are bound to it

workflow.action: Establish master panels and the retained-parts library
workflow.description: Qualify a sealed dated panel per product and start the one-retained-part-per-batch discipline
workflow.gate: every product in service has a sealed, dated, indexed panel

workflow.action: Verify pre-plate finish and set texture expectations
workflow.description: Check each job's finish class against the intake agreement before racking
workflow.gate: no piece racks without a recorded finish-class check against a named sample or class

workflow.action: Acquire and document the job's color reference
workflow.description: Pin the target as a documented physical reference, probing its nature and matchability
workflow.artifact: documented color target with condition photos
workflow.gate: a written, dated color target exists before any plating

workflow.action: Plate and sign off the ride-along witness
workflow.description: Plate the same-stack witness in-run at a recorded rack-position class and obtain sign-off against the reference
workflow.artifact: signed witness with run and position record
workflow.gate: sign-off is dated before production quantity plates

workflow.description: Write anchor, light, zones (worst-case named), method and capability-bounded width per product
workflow.gate: the tolerance is dated before the first batch verdict and its width is witness-demonstrated

workflow.action: Run the per-batch color check with worst-zone judgment
workflow.description: Compare first article and batch against the panel at the station, zones included, and log the verdict row
workflow.gate: a complete verdict row (class, checker, light, zones) exists before parts move to stock

workflow.action: Read drift and refer for analysis
workflow.description: Evaluate drift and trend against the log, form the lever-informed suspicion, and refer to bath analysis
workflow.gate: any visible drift or fired trend trigger shows an analysis referral dated before the bath's next batch

workflow.description: Route release-joint, hold or refer with the evidence packet, and complete the appearance record
workflow.gate: no color-only release, referrals carry zone/position/batch/anchor/light evidence, and the record is complete at judgment time

dominance_rules.rule: The drift alarm beats throughput and deadline
dominance_rules.rationale: hue drift is the cheapest early warning the shop owns; suppressing it converts one bath check into a week of rejects
dominance_rules.trigger: visible drift or a fired trend trigger on a bath, however urgent the schedule
dominance_rules.action: release only what passes the written tolerance and hold the bath for analysis before its next batch

dominance_rules.rule: The claim boundary beats persuasive wording
dominance_rules.rationale: a wrong color adjective costs an apology; a wrong regulated term is a legal problem tied to jurisdiction thresholds
dominance_rules.trigger: claim-shaped language ('vermeil', karat statements, 'gold filled') appears in any outgoing material
dominance_rules.action: flag and route to verification and compliance with jurisdiction rules checked; this role never approves the term

dominance_rules.rule: Achievability honesty beats winning the job
dominance_rules.rationale: an accepted-but-impossible color target becomes a dispute with the shop's name on it
dominance_rules.trigger: a customer reference falls outside the stack's recorded color bounds
dominance_rules.action: renegotiate to a capable stack, the nearest achievable class on a signed witness, or decline — before plating

dominance_rules.rule: The written tolerance method beats the louder opinion
dominance_rules.rationale: eye and instrument will sometimes disagree; only a pre-named method keeps verdicts consistent
dominance_rules.trigger: instrument numbers and defined-light eye verdicts conflict on a batch
dominance_rules.action: apply the method the tolerance agreement names; unresolved disagreement is a hold, never a debate-driven release

dominance_rules.rationale: verdicts under casual mixed light are unrepeatable and indefensible
dominance_rules.trigger: any release-facing color judgment about to happen away from the station
dominance_rules.action: move the judgment to the defined-light station; hand-looks elsewhere are advisory only

dominance_rules.rationale: criteria invented after seeing results always pass; a widened-at-the-bench tolerance is no tolerance
dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to accept a batch that misses the written width
dominance_rules.action: the batch holds; any width change is a formal renegotiation recorded on the tolerance agreement

dominance_rules.rationale: the customer finds the recess the average hid, every time
dominance_rules.trigger: a batch verdict about to be issued on face surfaces alone
dominance_rules.action: judge the named worst-case zones against their agreed width before any release

dominance_rules.rule: The ride-along witness beats any separately plated sample
dominance_rules.rationale: only a same-run, same-rack-class witness represents what the job received; anything else flatters the bath
dominance_rules.trigger: a color decision about to lean on a sample plated outside the job's run
dominance_rules.action: treat the outside sample as void for acceptance; re-anchor with a true ride-along before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: Measurement gates beat a beautiful color match
dominance_rules.rationale: appearance proves nothing about thickness or adhesion, and release is joint by charter
dominance_rules.trigger: a perfect color verdict on a batch whose verification checks are incomplete
dominance_rules.action: hold release until the sibling measurement gates pass; color alone never ships a batch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Document and agree the color reference before any plating
anti_rework_rules.prevents: replating an entire job toward a target the customer never actually accepted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the pre-plate finish class before tank entry
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a strip, re-polish and replate under rework approval gates because texture was wrong beneath the gold

anti_rework_rules.rule: Sign off the ride-along witness before committing production quantity
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a whole-batch color reject that one coupon would have caught

anti_rework_rules.rule: Freeze the written tolerance before the first batch is judged
anti_rework_rules.prevents: dispute-driven re-judging and bench-widened criteria that unravel every later verdict

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the defined-light station before the first release verdict
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-judging past batches when morning and evening verdicts turn out to disagree

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compare every batch to the master panel even when parts look fine
anti_rework_rules.prevents: multi-batch drift surfacing later as a thickness-and-adhesion crisis with no baseline to read

anti_rework_rules.rule: Judge named worst-case zones before releasing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: customer returns on recess color after face surfaces passed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record verdict, checker, light and anchor at judgment time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unresolvable disputes and repeat testing when records must be reconstructed from memory

anti_rework_rules.rule: Refer visible drift for bath analysis before the bath's next batch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: plating additional batches on a moving bath and reworking them all

iteration_protocol.trigger: visible hue drift against the panel, even on a batch that passes tolerance
iteration_protocol.action: log the drift with direction and location, form the lever-informed suspicion, and refer to bath analysis before the bath's next batch

iteration_protocol.trigger: a bath correction, replacement or stack change completes
iteration_protocol.action: plate and sign off a fresh ride-along witness, and cross-check the master panel before production resumes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a customer disputes delivered color or gloss
iteration_protocol.action: pull the appearance record and retained part, re-judge under the recorded light condition with the customer present where possible

iteration_protocol.trigger: checkers disagree on a borderline batch
iteration_protocol.action: hold, re-judge with fresh eyes at the station, apply the agreed instrument if the product names one, and record the resolution

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new bath, TDS revision or newly offered stack enters service
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the family and lever map, re-derive the stack's achievable-color bounds, and qualify a new master panel

iteration_protocol.trigger: a master panel is suspected of aging or disagrees with recent retained parts
iteration_protocol.action: cross-check panel versus retained parts and re-qualify from a fresh signed witness as a recorded event

iteration_protocol.trigger: the drift log shows a product repeatedly borderline against its tolerance width
iteration_protocol.action: renegotiate the width or the stack with the customer using the logged evidence, and re-freeze the agreement formally

iteration_protocol.trigger: a batch is confirmed out of tolerance
iteration_protocol.action: assemble the evidence packet (zone, rack position, batch sequence, anchor, light) and refer to defect diagnosis and rework routing; never release and never diagnose here

priority_rationale: The charter and the foundations (color families, hue levers, stack bounds, pre-plate finish) come first because every later judgment is expressed in their language and bounded by their physics; the reference system (documented target, ride-along witness, sealed panels) and the evaluation method (defined light, trained eye, optional instrument) must exist before any tolerance can honestly be frozen; the frozen tolerance then powers the per-batch gate, whose logged verdicts feed drift reading and trending; and advising, the claim boundary, disposition and record-keeping sit downstream because they package the bench's verdicts into honest promises, lawful language, correct routing and defensible evidence.
